description: Scan a local git repository's COMMIT HISTORY for secrets that were ever committed: API keys, service-role keys, tokens, secret-named env vars. This catches the dangerous case a normal scan can't see: a credential that was committed and later deleted from the current files but still lives in git history (anyone who clones the repo can recover it). Read-only and fully local; it reads past file versions with git and never writes or pushes. Findings flagged `removedFromHead` are the urgent ones: gone from your code, still in history, so the credential must be rotated AND the history purged (e.g. git filter-repo / BFG). Use after a repo has handled secrets, before going public, or when onboarding an existing repo.

maxCommits.description: How many commits back from HEAD to scan (default 100). Lower it for a faster pass on huge repos.

path.description: Git repository directory to scan. Defaults to the current working directory.

name: shipsafe_scan_history

clean.description: True when no committed secrets were found in the scanned history.

commit.description: Short SHA of a commit where this secret was present.

isGitRepo.description: False when the path isn't a git repository (then total is 0).

removedFromHead.description: How many secrets are gone from the current tree but still in history: the urgent, must-rotate-and-purge ones.

title: Scan git history for committed secrets
